title: Principles of Quantum Superposition
text:
The principle of superposition dictates that a quantum system exists in a combination of all its possible states simultaneously. A particle, such as an electron, is not fixed in a single location or energy level but occupies a probabilistic wave function across multiple possibilities concurrently.

Measurement fundamentally forces the wave function to 'collapse,' instantaneously resolving the system into one definitive, observable state. This unique interaction between observation and reality distinguishes quantum mechanics from classical physics, where objects are assumed to possess definite attributes at all times.
